Row 77 ng:front-I — refutation attempted along every requested axis; none succeeds. Verdict: NOT refuted (faithful given the disclosed FR-8/FR-6/FR-16 readings).

1. Clause set. Printed lemma (work/reviews/ng-front-i-source-excerpt-lines-1950-1953.tex.txt = sm-3:1950-1953): the single sentence "The front type-I moves preserve B." Nothing about D, w, d is asserted at statement level (ng:type-I-counts, sm-3:1964-1966, is a proof display). Every printed clause has a field and every field a printed clause; no extra or missing field.

2. Word pattern vs printed move. Printed (sm-3:1955-1956): "Each word l_m σ_{m−1} r_m or l_m σ_{m+1} r_m replaces one through-strand." Lean `IsTypeI` (work/lean/SM/FrontWords.lean:425-428): ∃ X Y m d, ((2 ≤ m ∧ W = X ++ [.l m d, .σ (m−1), .r m] ++ Y) ∨ (1 ≤ m ∧ W = X ++ [.l m d, .σ (m+1), .r m] ++ Y)) ∧ W' = X ++ Y. Expanded to primitives (Letter.step/act, FrontWords.lean:62-104): pattern 1 has the through-strand at position m−1 (cusp inserted below it), σ_{m−1} crosses it with the upper arm, r_m joins it with the lower arm, the upper arm exits at position m−1; typing forces d = through-strand bit, so both crossing arrows point the same way (positive crossing) and exactly one cusp is downward — the printed facts at sm-3:1958-1963. Pattern 2 is the mirror with the cusp inserted above. The orientation bit d is free and forced by typing (kernel-checked: `Word.run [.l 1 false, .σ 2, .r 1] [true] = some [true]`, `Word.run [.l 1 true, .σ 2, .r 1] [true] = none`; `writheFrom = 1`, `downCountFrom = 1` for both patterns, matching ng:type-I-counts). Concrete instantiation kernel-checked (/tmp/ref77_check.lean, `lake env lean` exit 0): W = [l 1 true, l 2 true, σ 1, r 2, r 1] (circle with a curl, closed by decide) and W = [l 1 true, l 1 false, σ 2, r 1, r 1] both satisfy `IsTypeI W [l 1 true, r 1]` with explicit witnesses. The index guards 2 ≤ m / 1 ≤ m are implied by typedness (`Letter.step` needs 1 ≤ idx, FrontWords.lean:100-103), so they narrow nothing. Importantly the pattern is not too broad either: the "wrong-crossing" curl l_2 σ_1 r_1 (incoming arc crossing the returning arc) is a closed word on a through-strand with syntactic ΔD = 1, Δw = −1 (kernel-checked), so it would change B by 2; it is NOT matched by `IsTypeI` (kernel-checked in /tmp/ref77_check3.lean), which is exactly the printed exclusion "An arbitrary front zigzag is not a type-I move" (sm-3:1968). Both printed variants, both curl sides and both orientations are covered; no fifth variant exists (a curl always has l left of r, and the crossing must be between the outer arcs for the printed positive-crossing/one-down-cusp facts).

The source defines the type-I move only as the two word patterns in its proof (sm-3:1955-1956), the section is explicitly "Ordinary certificates for the local front moves" on Rutherford's words (sm-3:1900-1919), and the lemma's only consumer, ng:finite-word item 1 (blueprint/AXIOM_REGISTRY.md:83-92), applies it to "an actual finite front word".
